record.original_question: Let n be a positive integer, and let (p_α) be a prescribed collection of numbers indexed by the nonempty increasing index sets α from {1, 2, ..., n}. Does there exist an n × n matrix A such that every principal minor of A matches the prescribed data, that is, A[α] = p_α for all nonempty α?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. For a subset $\alpha \subseteq \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ and an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ (with entries in $\mathbb{C}$, say), let $A[\alpha]$ denote the principal minor of $A$ indexed by $\alpha$, i.e., the determinant of the submatrix obtained by selecting the rows and columns whose indices lie in $\alpha$. Given a prescribed collection of scalars $(p_\alpha)_{\emptyset \neq \alpha \subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}}$, give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an $n\times n$ matrix $A$ such that 
$$A[\alpha] = p_\alpha \quad \text{for every nonempty } \alpha \subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}.$$
Equivalently, characterize the image of the map sending an $n\times n$ matrix to the tuple of all its $2^n-1$ nonempty principal minors.
artifact.status_search_result: The principal minor assignment problem has been studied extensively. For symmetric matrices, Holtz and Sturmfels (Principal minors, Part II) gave algebraic relations (hyperdeterminantal relations) characterizing the image, and Oeding (2011) proved these relations cut out the variety set-theoretically; efficient algorithms exist for the symmetric case. For general (non-symmetric) matrices, the problem remains only partially understood: recent work (e.g., on magnitude-symmetric matrices and signed DPPs, 2018–2024) provides further partial results, but a complete characterization of all realizable tuples for general square matrices is not established.

status_evidence.title: Principal minors, Part II: The principal minor assignment problem
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions are studied for a collection of 2^n numbers to be the principal minors of an n×n matrix.
status_evidence.claim: The symmetric principal minor assignment problem has been characterized via hyperdeterminantal-type relations.

status_evidence.title: An efficient algorithm for the symmetric principal minor assignment problem
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient algorithm reconstructing a symmetric matrix from its principal minors.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic solution exists in the symmetric case.

status_evidence.title: Learning Signed Determinantal Point Processes through the Principal Minor Assignment Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Studies PMAP for signed DPP kernels, extending beyond the symmetric PSD case.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions to broader classes of matrices have been pursued, indicating the general case is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing and Testing Principal Minor Equivalence of Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Recent 2024 work on principal minor equivalence, indicating continuing research activity.
status_evidence.claim: Problem remains active research, particularly outside the symmetric setting.
